findings.issue_text: assignment_source kwarg passed to installation.sync_assignee_outbound() but the abstract method signature and concrete provider implementations (Jira, GitHub, VSTS, etc.) were never updated, causing TypeError on first real outbound assignee sync

queued field should use field(default_factory=timezone.now) plus explicit encode/decode in to_dict/from_dict

Status-sync cycles are not prevented: sync_status_outbound's assignment_source parameter is dead code, no call site passes it and status sync paths don't thread a source, so inbound status changes still ping-pong back outbound
Dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated at import time so every instance shares the process-start timestamp; should use field(default_factory=timezone.now)

`sync_status_outbound` abstract signature adds an `assignment_source` parameter that no caller passes and no implementer is updated for; it will cause TypeError for implementers not declaring it or be silently ignored, so it should be removed or wired through a real call path

queued: datetime = timezone.now() default is evaluated once at class-definition time, so instances without explicit queued carry the process-start timestamp instead of the actual queue time
should_sync signature change to two positional args breaks existing subclass overrides with single-parameter signatures, raising TypeError and killing the sync task

sync_status_outbound gained an assignment_source parameter that no call site passes and status-inbound sync does not tag assignments, so status sync cycle prevention is only half realized (dead forward-plumbing)
from_dict swallows malformed payloads and returns None, which the caller treats as 'no source', silently re-enabling the sync loop with no log marking the parse failure
from_dict reconstructs AssignmentSource from unvalidated dict (Celery task kwarg), allowing forged integration_id values that can suppress or defeat outbound assignee sync
queued dataclass field default uses timezone.now() evaluated once at class definition, so all instances share the process start time instead of actual queue time

AssignmentSource dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` uses a class-definition-time default, so all instances share one frozen import-time timestamp instead of per-instance time (needs default_factory)
Test `test_to_dict` asserts only `result.get('queued') is not None`, which passes regardless of whether the queued value is correct, stale, or wrong type, providing no real verification

`sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes AssignmentSource.to_dict() output containing a datetime as a Celery apply_async kwarg; the default JSON serializer cannot encode datetime, raising EncodeError so the outbound sync task is never enqueued and legitimate assignee sync breaks when assignment_source exists

The new test `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` runs with eager task execution (self.tasks()), bypassing serialization, so it cannot catch the datetime serialization failure
AssignmentSource.from_dict does not validate types, so it would return an instance whose `queued` is a string, making its validation illusory

No test covers the propagation path where an AssignmentSource from a different integration should still allow outbound sync; only the suppression branch is tested, so a regression over-suppressing sourced syncs would be invisible

The deassign path's new `assignment_source` plumbing is untested: no test asserts that deassign with an assignment_source suppresses the outbound unassign, so mis-wiring the deassign call site passes the suite
`sync_status_outbound`'s new `assignment_source` parameter has no caller and no test — speculative generality adding a dead parameter to all provider implementations
Minor naming nits: typo in `test_from_dict_inalid_data` and misnamed `test_from_dict_empty_array` which tests an empty dict, not an array

from_dict performs no datetime parsing, so a JSON round-trip rehydrates queued as a str, silently violating the type contract
should_sync signature change to (self, attribute, sync_source=...) breaks every existing override that doesn't accept the new parameter, raising TypeError at sync time with no compatibility period

sync_status_outbound abstract method gains an assignment_source parameter that no caller in the diff passes, indicating an incomplete rollout of cycle-prevention design so status-sync loops remain possible
from_dict swallows TypeError for non-dict or wrong-typed input and returns None, degrading to treat-as-user-originated and re-enabling the sync cycle the PR exists to prevent

adjudication_records.issue_text: assignment_source kwarg passed to installation.sync_assignee_outbound() but the abstract method signature and concrete provider implementations (Jira, GitHub, VSTS, etc.) were never updated, causing TypeError on first real outbound assignee sync

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Celery task to call `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` (src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py), but the PR does not show any corresponding update to the `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound` API in the base mixin (src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py). If existing concrete installations/providers implement `sync_assignee_outbound` without `**kwargs` or the new kwarg, this new call site will raise `TypeError: got an unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source'` at runtime. The added tests patch the method with a mock, so they wouldn’t catch a signature mismatch in real implementations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests only pass because @mock.patch.object(ExampleIntegration, "sync_assignee_outbound") hides the signature mismatch; sync_status_outbound was updated but not sync_assignee_outbound, showing asymmetry was missed

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show a verifiable signature mismatch being “hidden” by the mock. While `sync_status_outbound` was updated to take an explicit `assignment_source` parameter, the diff does not show the definition of `sync_assignee_outbound` (it may already accept `**kwargs`), nor does it show any concrete integration implementation with an incompatible signature. The tests’ use of `@mock.patch.object(ExampleIntegration, "sync_assignee_outbound")` could theoretically mask a mismatch, but that claim is not provable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssignmentSource.queued default `timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class-definition/import time, so every instance without explicit queued gets a frozen import timestamp
to_dict() puts raw datetime into Celery task kwargs; JSON serialization converts it to string and from_dict does no type coercion, silently reconstructing queued as str causing TypeError in consumers
queued field should use field(default_factory=timezone.now) plus explicit encode/decode in to_dict/from_dict

Status-sync cycles are not prevented: sync_status_outbound's assignment_source parameter is dead code, no call site passes it and status sync paths don't thread a source, so inbound status changes still ping-pong back outbound

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `assignment_source` parameter to `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_status_outbound(...)` and extends `should_sync(..., sync_source=...)` with cycle-prevention logic, but the only new threading of `AssignmentSource` shown in the diff is for assignee sync (`sync_group_assignee_outbound` -> task -> `installation.should_sync(..., parsed_assignment_source)` -> `sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`). There are no corresponding diff changes that pass an `AssignmentSource` into status-sync paths or call `should_sync` for status with a source, so within this PR the new status parameter appears unused and the cycle-prevention logic is not applied to status sync.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated at import time so every instance shares the process-start timestamp; should use field(default_factory=timezone.now)

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` (new file `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`), the dataclass field is defined as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`, which calls `timezone.now()` at import/class-definition time. This means all `AssignmentSource` instances created without an explicit `queued` will share the same timestamp for the lifetime of the process, instead of capturing creation time. Using `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` would avoid this shared default.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test only asserts suppression case; missing test that non-matching AssignmentSource still propagates assignee sync to other integrations

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` to suppress outbound syncing when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (to prevent sync cycles). Tests added include a suppression case (`test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration`) and existing propagation cases where `assignment_source=None` (`test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign`, `..._unassign`). However, there is no test covering the nontrivial edge case where `assignment_source` is present but refers to a *different* integration, which should still allow propagation per the comment in `should_sync`. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test for the inbound-deassign cycle (sync_group_assignee_inbound's deassign with assignment_source branch)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new behavior path in `sync_group_assignee_inbound`: when `assign` is false it now calls `GroupAssignee.objects.deassign(group, assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration))` (previously deassigned without `assignment_source`). This interacts with the newly-added cycle-prevention logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` that suppresses outbound sync when the source integration matches the target integration. The added tests cover outbound assign cycle-prevention (`test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration`) and basic outbound assign/unassign calls expecting `assignment_source=None`, but there is no test that exercises the inbound *deassign* branch (and verifies it does not trigger outbound sync due to matching `assignment_source`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict performs no type coercion, so a payload with integration_id as a string silently breaks cycle suppression via the Celery JSON serialization path

adjudication.rationale: `AssignmentSource.from_dict` simply does `cls(**input_dict)` and catches only `ValueError`/`TypeError`, but dataclasses don’t enforce type annotations at runtime. So `{"integration_id": "123"}` would produce an `AssignmentSource` with a string `integration_id`, and `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(...): sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` would then fail to detect a cycle. However, in the shown call path (`AssignmentSource.to_dict()` -> Celery task kwargs), `integration_id` originates as an `int` and JSON would normally preserve it as a number, so the claim that Celery serialization *will* turn it into a string isn’t directly verifiable from this diff; it’s more of a robustness/validation gap than a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Malformed assignment_source_dict silently downgrades to None (sync everything) instead of failing safe; no logging on parse failure in sync_assignee_outbound task

adjudication.rationale: In `sync_assignee_outbound` the new `assignment_source_dict` is parsed via `AssignmentSource.from_dict(...)`, which returns `None` on `ValueError`/`TypeError` (and on missing required keys). The task then calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`; if parsing failed, `parsed_assignment_source` becomes `None`, skipping the new cycle-prevention check in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` (`if sync_source and sync_source.integration_id == ...: return False`). This means a malformed `assignment_source_dict` can unintentionally re-enable outbound sync (including potential sync-cycles) and the failure is silent (no logging/metric in the task).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dataclass field default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` in assignment_source.py is evaluated once at module import, so all AssignmentSource instances share a frozen timestamp

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`, the dataclass defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. This calls `timezone.now()` at class definition (module import) time, so all `AssignmentSource` instances that don’t pass `queued` will share the same frozen timestamp. In dataclasses this should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to evaluate per-instance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Passing `assignment_source.to_dict()` (containing a datetime) as a Celery apply_async kwarg raises TypeError with the default JSON serializer, so the outbound assignee sync task never enqueues and assignee changes silently fail to propagate

`sync_status_outbound` signature was widened to accept `assignment_source` but no implementation, caller, or inbound path uses it, and cycle prevention covers only assignee sync, leaving status-sync loops unguarded

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `assignment_source` to `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(...)` and uses it to prevent cycles (by comparing `sync_source.integration_id` to `self.org_integration.integration_id`), but only the assignee outbound path is updated to pass a source (`sync_assignee_outbound` parses `assignment_source_dict` and calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`). Separately, the abstract `sync_status_outbound(...)` signature is widened to accept `assignment_source`, yet this diff shows no callers updated to pass it and no status-sync cycle-prevention wired up via `should_sync(..., sync_source=...)`. This is an incomplete/unused interface extension rather than a verifiable runtime defect from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anti-cycle invariant is enforced only at one `should_sync` call site; all other callers pass no `sync_source` (defaulting to None), so the invariant is not a property of the sync layer

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an optional `sync_source`/`AssignmentSource` parameter to `IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync` and enforces the anti-cycle check only when that argument is provided (`IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` returns False if `sync_source.integration_id` matches `self.org_integration.integration_id`). In the shown changes, only the assignee outbound path is updated to pass this source (`sync_assignee_outbound` parses `assignment_source_dict` and calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`). Because the parameter defaults to `None`, any other existing `should_sync(attribute)` callers (not shown here) would continue to bypass the anti-cycle guard unless updated to pass a source, making the invariant dependent on call-site discipline rather than enforced universally by the sync layer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Region-silo model groupassignee.py now imports integration code at module top level, breaking the established deferred-import pattern and risking import cycles if assignment_source.py later imports models

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/models/groupassignee.py` (a `region_silo_model`), the diff adds a new top-level import `from sentry.integrations.services.assignment_source import AssignmentSource` and then threads this type through `assign(..., assignment_source=...)` / `deassign(..., assignment_source=...)`. The file already uses deferred imports inside methods for integration-related functionality (`from sentry.integrations.utils import sync_group_assignee_outbound`), so pulling an integrations-service module into the module import graph is a concrete architecture/coupling concern. However, the diff does not show an actual import cycle or runtime break today: `assignment_source.py` only references models under `TYPE_CHECKING` and does not import `GroupAssignee`/models at runtime. The stated “breaking behavior” is speculative, but the cross-layer import is real and reviewable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Placing the assignment_source dataclass under integrations/services creates implicit coupling where region-silo model code depends on an integrations package module for a core domain concept, blocking future moves of assignment provenance into a model field

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `src/sentry/models/groupassignee.py` (a `region_silo_model`) now imports `AssignmentSource` from `sentry.integrations.services.assignment_source` and threads it through `assign/deassign` into `sync_group_assignee_outbound`. This does introduce a concrete dependency from core model code into the `integrations.services` package (cross-domain coupling). The claim about "blocking future moves ... into a model field" is speculative, but the coupling concern itself is diff-grounded and architectural rather than a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at module import time so all instances share the same timestamp; should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AssignmentSource` dataclass, the field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` sets the default value by calling `timezone.now()` at class definition (module import) time, so every `AssignmentSource()` created without an explicit `queued` will share the same timestamp. This is a real correctness bug; it should use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to compute a fresh timestamp per instance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `from_dict` round-trips through `asdict` keeping `queued` as datetime, which fails JSON serialization when passed as a Celery task kwarg, and `from_dict` silently accepts a string `queued` from other producers with no format validation

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` using `dataclasses.asdict`, which will include `queued` as a `datetime` object (see `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` and `to_dict = asdict(self)`). That dict is then passed directly into a Celery task kwarg (`sync_group_assignee_outbound` -> `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(... assignment_source_dict=assignment_source.to_dict())`). With JSON-based task serialization (a common/default Celery setup), a raw `datetime` in kwargs is not serializable and would break task dispatch. Additionally, `AssignmentSource.from_dict` just does `cls(**input_dict)` and only catches `ValueError`/`TypeError`, so it will accept a string `queued` without validation/conversion, yielding an instance with an incorrect `queued` type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sync_status_outbound` abstract signature adds an `assignment_source` parameter that no caller passes and no implementer is updated for; it will cause TypeError for implementers not declaring it or be silently ignored, so it should be removed or wired through a real call path

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the abstract `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_status_outbound` signature to accept `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None` (and keeps `**kwargs`), but this PR only wires `assignment_source` through the assignee sync path (`sync_assignee_outbound`, `GroupAssignee.assign/deassign`, `should_sync`). There is no diff-shown call path passing `assignment_source` into `sync_status_outbound`, so adding the parameter here looks unused/incomplete within this PR. However, the claim that it "will cause TypeError" and that "no implementer is updated" cannot be verified from the diff alone (implementers/callers may exist elsewhere), and the added parameter is optional with a default and `**kwargs`, so it is not a clearly verifiable break based solely on this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cycle-prevention check only blocks self-loops (same integration_id) and does not prevent two-integration ping-pong sync loops, since there is no hop counter or staleness cutoff despite the comment claiming sync-cycles are prevented

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s cycle-prevention logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` only skips syncing when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (i.e., the same integration) and explicitly says it “should still allow other integrations to propagate changes outward.” There is no hop counter/staleness check in `AssignmentSource` usage (it includes a `queued` timestamp but it’s not consulted anywhere in this diff), so the finding is correct that this does not address potential multi-integration ping-pong loops. However, whether that causes an actual infinite loop depends on inbound behavior outside this diff (e.g., how external systems trigger inbound updates), so it’s best classified as an incomplete edge-case/design concern rather than a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `from_dict` returns `None` on malformed input, conflating 'no source provided' with 'source provided but corrupt', which silently re-enables the self-loop sync cycle the diff is meant to prevent; it should raise or log instead of collapsing to `None`

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AssignmentSource.from_dict` intentionally returns `None` on invalid/missing fields (services/assignment_source.py), and `sync_assignee_outbound` treats a parse failure the same as “no source provided” by passing `None` into `installation.should_sync(...)` (tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py). In `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync`, the self-loop prevention only triggers when `sync_source` is non-`None` (mixins/issues.py). So if a malformed `assignment_source_dict` is ever provided, the cycle-prevention check is skipped and outbound sync may proceed. This is a real, diff-grounded robustness concern, but the diff doesn’t establish that malformed input can occur in normal operation (the dict is produced internally via `to_dict()`), so it’s not a clearly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: celery task sync_assignee_outbound receives a dict containing a datetime (queued field) via apply_async kwargs, which the default JSON serializer cannot encode, causing EncodeError and the task to never run

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` (via `asdict`) which includes the `queued: datetime` field, and `sync_group_assignee_outbound()` passes that dict directly into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={... "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict() ...})`. A raw `datetime` in Celery task kwargs will not be JSON-serializable under the default JSON serializer, causing an encode error and preventing the task from being enqueued/run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: queued: datetime = timezone.now() default is evaluated once at class-definition time, so instances without explicit queued carry the process-start timestamp instead of the actual queue time

adjudication.rationale: In the new dataclass `AssignmentSource` (src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py), the field is declared as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. That calls `timezone.now()` at import/class-definition time, so every instance created without an explicit `queued` will get the same frozen timestamp (process start/import time) rather than the actual creation/queue time. Dataclasses require `field(default_factory=...)` for dynamic defaults.

adjudication_records.issue_text: should_sync signature change to two positional args breaks existing subclass overrides with single-parameter signatures, raising TypeError and killing the sync task

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `should_sync` to accept a new optional parameter (`sync_source`) and updates at least one call site to pass it (`installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` in `sync_assignee_outbound`). If any existing integration subclass overrides `should_sync(self, attribute)` with the old single-arg signature, that override would not accept the second argument and could raise `TypeError` at runtime. adjudication_records.issue_text: sync_status_outbound gained an assignment_source parameter that no call site passes and status-inbound sync does not tag assignments, so status sync cycle prevention is only half realized (dead forward-plumbing)

In this diff there is no analogous status-outbound task/update passing an `AssignmentSource` into `should_sync`/`sync_status_outbound`, so the added parameter appears to be forward-plumbing without effect (incomplete implementation rather than a correctness break, since it's optional).

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict swallows malformed payloads and returns None, which the caller treats as 'no source', silently re-enabling the sync loop with no log marking the parse failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AssignmentSource.from_dict` intentionally swallowing `ValueError`/`TypeError` and returning `None` (new file `assignment_source.py`), and the Celery task `sync_assignee_outbound` treats `None` as “no source” (`parsed_assignment_source = ... else None`) and then calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`. Since `should_sync` only blocks cycles when `sync_source` is present and matches the same integration id, a malformed `assignment_source_dict` would silently disable the new cycle-prevention check with no logging. However, within this diff the only producer (`sync_group_assignee_outbound`) passes `assignment_source.to_dict()` which should be well-formed, so it’s not a provable defect in normal flow; it’s a robustness/observability gap for unexpected/legacy/malformed task payloads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict reconstructs AssignmentSource from unvalidated dict (Celery task kwarg), allowing forged integration_id values that can suppress or defeat outbound assignee sync

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `sync_assignee_outbound` accepts a raw `assignment_source_dict` (Celery kwargs) and `AssignmentSource.from_dict` reconstructs it with `cls(**input_dict)` and no validation beyond type/shape errors. That value is then trusted in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source=...)` to suppress outbound sync when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`. So, if an attacker could enqueue the task with arbitrary kwargs, they could forge an `integration_id` to disable outbound assignee syncing. However, the diff itself only shows internal code paths generating this dict via `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` (e.g., `sync_group_assignee_outbound`), and does not establish that untrusted parties can supply Celery kwargs, so a concrete security defect is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: queued dataclass field default uses timezone.now() evaluated once at class definition, so all instances share the process start time instead of actual queue time

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`, the dataclass field is defined as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`, which calls `timezone.now()` at class definition/import time. That value becomes the shared default for all instances that don’t explicitly pass `queued`, so multiple `AssignmentSource()` objects will incorrectly get the same timestamp rather than the actual creation/queue time. This should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test `test_to_dict` asserts only `result.get('queued') is not None`, which passes regardless of whether the queued value is correct, stale, or wrong type, providing no real verification

This is a real, diff-grounded test weakness, but not a runtime defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes AssignmentSource.to_dict() output containing a datetime as a Celery apply_async kwarg; the default JSON serializer cannot encode datetime, raising EncodeError so the outbound sync task is never enqueued and legitimate assignee sync breaks when assignment_source exists

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new test `test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration` runs with eager task execution (self.tasks()), bypassing serialization, so it cannot catch the datetime serialization failure

So the test as written does not validate that the enqueued payload is safely serializable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssignmentSource.from_dict does not validate types, so it would return an instance whose `queued` is a string, making its validation illusory

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.from_dict`, the implementation is `return cls(**input_dict)` and only catches `ValueError`/`TypeError`. That means a payload like `{"source_name": "x", "integration_id": 1, "queued": "2026-01-01"}` would successfully construct an `AssignmentSource` with `queued` set to a string despite the `datetime` type annotation—no runtime type validation exists in this diff. However, the diff does not show any code path that relies on `queued` being a `datetime` (it’s never read/used), so this is more a robustness/validation concern than a clearly verifiable defect in behavior introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test covers the propagation path where an AssignmentSource from a different integration should still allow outbound sync; only the suppression branch is tested, so a regression over-suppressing sourced syncs would be invisible

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssignmentSource.to_dict() puts a raw datetime into Celery task kwargs, which fails JSON serialization under Celery's default JSON serializer, so the outbound sync task is never enqueued and inbound assignments fail their outbound propagation

Whether this actually “fails JSON serialization under Celery’s default JSON serializer” and prevents enqueueing is not verifiable from the diff alone (serializer configuration/behavior isn’t shown), so the finding overstates certainty, but the underlying serialization compatibility concern is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: queued: datetime = timezone.now() is a class-definition-time default evaluated once at module import, so every instance carries the process-import time instead of the actual queued time

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` (new file `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`), the dataclass field is defined as `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. In Python dataclasses, that expression is evaluated once at class definition/import time, so all instances created without an explicit `queued` will share the same timestamp (the process import time), rather than the actual creation time. This should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to get a per-instance timestamp.

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict performs no datetime parsing, so a JSON round-trip rehydrates queued as a str, silently violating the type contract

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` (new file), `queued` is annotated as `datetime`, but `from_dict` simply does `return cls(**input_dict)` with no coercion/validation. If `queued` comes back from a JSON/task-serializer round-trip as a string (common for datetimes), the dataclass will accept it and `queued` will be a `str` at runtime, silently violating the stated type contract. The diff also shows `to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)`, which will include the `queued` value, increasing the likelihood this dict is serialized/deserialized (e.g., passed through `sync_assignee_outbound` task kwargs).

adjudication_records.issue_text: sync_status_outbound abstract method gains an assignment_source parameter that no caller in the diff passes, indicating an incomplete rollout of cycle-prevention design so status-sync loops remain possible

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict swallows TypeError for non-dict or wrong-typed input and returns None, degrading to treat-as-user-originated and re-enabling the sync cycle the PR exists to prevent

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.from_dict`, any `TypeError`/`ValueError` while unpacking (`cls(**input_dict)`) returns `None`. In `sync_assignee_outbound`, a `None` `parsed_assignment_source` means `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` will not hit the cycle-prevention check (`if sync_source and sync_source.integration_id == ...: return False`), so malformed `assignment_source_dict` could bypass the new protection. However, within this diff the only producer (`sync_group_assignee_outbound`) passes `assignment_source.to_dict()` (a valid dict) or `None`, so the problematic path requires an external/malformed task invocation and is not a directly verifiable broken behavior from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssignmentSource.queued uses timezone.now() as a dataclass default evaluated at class-definition time, so all instances get the module import time instead of the actual queue time; should use field(default_factory=timezone.now)

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`, the dataclass defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. This calls `timezone.now()` at import/class-definition time, so every `AssignmentSource()` created without an explicit `queued` will share the same timestamp (the module import time), not the actual time it was created/queued. Dataclasses require `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` to compute a fresh value per instance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cycle protection fails on the real task path: to_dict emits queued as a datetime, celery JSON serialization turns it into a string, and from_dict then raises TypeError which is swallowed and returns None, so the anti-loop guard is bypassed in production and sync loops can re-occur

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` uses `dataclasses.asdict`, which will include `queued` as whatever value it holds, but `AssignmentSource.from_dict()` simply does `return cls(**input_dict)` and dataclasses do not runtime-enforce type annotations. So even if Celery serialized `queued` to a string, `cls(**input_dict)` would still succeed (no `TypeError`) and the anti-loop guard in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` would still receive a non-None `AssignmentSource` with `integration_id` available for comparison. The claimed `TypeError`/`None` path only happens when required keys are missing or keys are unexpected, which isn’t shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: from_dict returns None on any malformed payload with zero logging, silently degrading cycle protection to a no-op; should at least log a warning with the offending payload

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AssignmentSource.from_dict` intentionally swallowing `ValueError`/`TypeError` and returning `None` with no logging (`except (ValueError, TypeError): return None`). In `sync_assignee_outbound`, a `None` parse result is then passed to `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`, which disables the new cycle-prevention check (since it only triggers when `sync_source` is non-None). That said, the only producer in this diff is `assignment_source.to_dict()` (in `sync_group_assignee_outbound`), so malformed payloads aren’t evidenced here; lack of logging is a diagnosability/robustness concern rather than a verifiable functional defect from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inbound assignment failures leave Sentry's local state silently out of sync when the user can't be matched — group remains unassigned with only an info-level log and no visible sync error or user surfacing

adjudication.rationale: In `sync_group_assignee_inbound`, when a matching Sentry user can’t be found for the inbound assignee email (`user = users_by_id.get(user_id)`), the code only logs `logger.info("assignee-not-found-inbound", ...)` and otherwise leaves the group unchanged (no assignment and no error/sync-failure surfaced). This can result in the external system showing an assignee while Sentry remains unassigned without any visible indication beyond an info log. The diff doesn’t add any handling for this case (it only adds `assignment_source` propagation), so the concern is real but more of a UX/observability gap than a correctness defect proven by the change.
